u0: At this point no triggered requirement is outstanding: any client arrival has been answered, any taken order has been carried through its required steps, and there is no unfinished delivery. The agent is up to date and can wait for the next client or begin a new order when one arrives. This is the neutral, fully caught-up condition of the task rather than a permanent stopping point.
u1: An order has been taken, but the agent has not yet fetched food for it. The open requirements are to take a portion into its hands and prepare it at the stove; after preparation, the food must still be served to the waiting client. These duties persist until the corresponding events occur.
u10: A client has arrived and still needs their order taken, while an open order still requires food to be held and already-prepared food still requires serving. The food-fetch requirement and the delivery requirement are both unresolved. Taking the new order can add its own later fetch, prepare, and serve duties, so all outstanding work must be completed.
u11: A client has arrived and still needs their order taken, and an order already in progress still needs food to be fetched. The arrival duty and the food-fetch duty are both outstanding. Once food is held, the fetch requirement is cleared, while the waiting client's order still has to be taken.
u12: Three service duties remain unresolved: food still has to be fetched, food still has to be prepared at the stove, and a prepared portion still has to be served. Satisfying one of these duties does not by itself clear the others. All of them must be completed.
u13: Food for an open order still needs to be prepared, and food that has already been prepared still needs to be served. The preparation duty and the serving duty are both unresolved, and completing one does not clear the other. The agent must ensure the required stove preparation happens and that a prepared meal reaches the client.
u14: All four stages of the service requirements are currently outstanding: a waiting client still needs their order taken, food still needs to be fetched, food still needs to be prepared, and prepared food still needs to be served. None of these duties has been cleared, so the agent must work through the entire sequence. Because they are independent requirements, progress on one stage does not erase the others.
u15: A client has arrived and still needs their order taken, while an open order still requires food to be prepared and prepared food still requires serving. The order-taking, stove-preparation, and delivery duties are all unresolved. Completing one of them will not by itself clear the other outstanding requirements.
u2: An order is open and food has already been obtained for it, but the food has not yet been prepared. The remaining work is to bring raw food to the stove, prepare it, and then deliver it to the waiting client. If the portion has slipped away since it was picked up, another portion must be obtained before preparation.
u3: The food for an open order has already been prepared, so the fetching and preparation steps are satisfied. What remains is to serve the prepared food to the waiting client; if the prepared portion is not currently in hand, it must be recovered first. Serving clears the final outstanding duty for this order.
u4: An order has been taken and food has been prepared, but the agent still has an unresolved food-holding requirement and a prepared meal still needs to be served. The prepared portion is not in the agent's hands, so it must regain food and then deliver the meal to the client. Both duties must be cleared.
u5: An order has been taken, and the only unresolved requirement recorded for it is that the agent must eventually hold food. Fetching a portion is the immediate duty; once food is in hand, this fetch requirement is cleared. No separate preparation or serving duty is currently outstanding here.
u6: A client has arrived and their order has not yet been taken. The agent must take that order, which then opens the later fetch, prepare, and serve steps for the client. Until the order is taken, this arrival requirement remains unresolved.
u7: Two requirements are open: a client arrival still needs to be answered by taking an order, and food that has already been prepared still needs to be served. Taking the order does not satisfy the prepared-food delivery, and serving does not satisfy the untaken order. Both must be completed.
u8: A client has arrived and still needs their order taken, while an open order still requires food to be fetched and prepared. The state carries three unfinished duties: take the waiting client's order, obtain food, and prepare it at the stove. Once the food is prepared, serving will also become due.
u9: A client has arrived and still needs their order taken, while an order already in progress still needs its food prepared. Food has already been obtained for that preparation requirement, so the stove step is the next part of that duty. After preparation, the resulting meal will still need to be served.
